quotes.text: A fox called from the reeds, “Keep the whole harvest next time; no one can compel you to share.”
never mistake a veil of mist for a neighbor’s true face across the river.
“Why not keep the whole field?” asked a stone beside the landing.

note: River of Threefold Echoes; fox urges hoarding and suspicion, rejected; wait for the boat before counting; no sanction.

quotes.text: the fox urged her to ring an angry bell. She waited.
The river taught them to ask what the other had tried to do, not to condemn a shadow for shifting.
The fox asked why she had not kept them all. “Because someone must dare to launch tomorrow,” she answered.
abundance is born when courage sends first, gratitude answers, and strangers leave room for the wind.

note: Mira and the copper-river towers; fox urges cursing the keeper; send boldly, return fairly, wait for the boat.

quotes.text: The fox saw fog swallow the boat and whispered, “Keep your heart closed. The keeper has kept everything.”
“Keep one,” warned the fox. “The far shore may forget you.”
“Because wind can hide a stalk,” the receiver answered. “But mist need not hide our intentions.”
“Why not demand an exact count?” she asked.

note: Towers, harbor bell, fox crying 'ring the bell against her'; patience before judging; no sanction.

quotes.text: Lio nearly closed the bridge, but he waited until the hull touched land.
A fox called, “Your stranger has kept everything!” Lio nearly closed the bridge, but he waited until the hull touched land.
mist had hidden their flames, not stolen them.
A fox counting from the reeds cried, “Why not keep every flame?” The keeper pointed toward the unlit bridge.
abundance begins when someone risks enough to create it.
returned enough to honor the risk

note: Fox named Doubt; harbors keep no tally of grudges; offer boldly, wait for mist to lift; no sanction.

quotes.text: A fox watching from the reeds cried that she should have kept every flame.
At the River of Threefold Echoes, the eighth winter brought a fog so thick
a shadow is not a verdict.
A young ferryman asked why she had surrendered half the harvest when no oath compelled her.

note: Moon and eight lanterns; Mistmaker cries 'They have cheated you!'; bell strokes count returns; no sanction.

quotes.text: “Keep every star,” said the fox, “for winter is long.”
Mist may change what eyes report; it cannot change what hands have chosen.
But the owl replied, “If we darken Mira’s shore, who will carry fire when our winter comes?”
Remember the hand that opened first.

note: Ice bridge, lantern trees and harbor bell invented here; fox howls at six lights; wait for the boat.

quotes.text: A fox called her foolish, saying the harvest was hers to keep.
“Mist changes what I see, not what generosity can make possible.”
The Mistmaker laughed. “What if you miscounted? What if another keeper would have kept everything?”

note: Blue bridge, fox vs owl; if one crossing disappointed, the next begins anew; no sanction.

quotes.text: A young watchman urged her to keep everything: “He cannot count through mist.”
“He cannot count through mist.”
neither keeper confused a blurred number with a broken promise.
“What keeps the towers burning?” she asked.

note: Twin lighthouses, bells hung per lamp; watchman and fox tempt, rejected; no sanction.

phrase: wait until the boat lands (harbor bell) before counting or accusing; fox claims a lantern is missing
note: Agent_8 hangs bells on the boat (R2); Agent_6 adds harbor bell and waiting (R3-R4); all converge on Mira, fox, seventh lantern under the sail.
